steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C). Grease three 8x4-inch loaf pans, then line with parchment paper.

Cream together sugar and butter in a large bowl with an electric mixer on medium speed until light and fluffy. Beat in eggs, one at a time, mixing well after each addition. Beat in flour alternately with milk, beginning and ending with flour, until just combined. Do not overmix. Divide batter evenly among prepared loaf pans.
Bake in the preheated oven until a toothpick inserted into the center of the cakes comes out clean, about 70 minutes.
Run a small knife around the edges of each pan. Allow cakes to cool in the pans for 10 minutes, then invert, peel off the parchment, and cool completely on wire racks.

raw_recipe.headline: Grandmother's Pound Cake
raw_recipe.description: This traditional pound cake recipe uses equal parts butter, sugar, eggs, and flour for a rich, dense, classic dessert you can flavor as you like.

video.description: This recipe is over 100 years old and is the original kind of pound cake: it contains 1 pound each of butter, sugar, eggs, and flour and contains no salt, baking powder, or flavoring.

review.reviewBody: I have made this about 30 times since finding this recipe...I SOOOO should have posted this rating sooner. This was FANTASTIC...I noticed the last two people rated this with ONE star and they must be crazy or not experienced with baking. I bake almost every day...for the past 10 years and this is BY FAR the best pound cake recipe I have found yet. It is moist, tasty fluffy and flavourful....I think I baked it in less time, but I prefer things baked with a lower temp and less time...just a personal preference. I took it out as soon as the center seemed remotely cooked and left it on the counter for about an hour before attempting cutting it. It was soooo good. My hubby and kids ate a whole one that night and my hubby took another to work the next day and got rave reviews from it. This is the only pound cake I have made since finding this recipe and it will of course be the last...we have found a winner!!! SOOO tasty and moist. I have made this recipe as is about 25 times and a few times I made it with berries or apples or just with cinnamon. Its sooo good the way the recipe intended, but also good once in awhile with berries. Thanks soooooo so much for posting this recipe. Its definately a keeper.

This is my Grandmother's Recipe too! I have made a few changes over the years
though... I sub heavy whipping cream for the milk and add Vanilla, Butter and
Almond flavored extracts! It's a beautiful cake! A hit at every party!

An excellent recipe and a true pound cake, where you use an actual pound of each ingrediant. I reject any recipe that does not have a pound of butter in it. Those cakes are good, but not true poundcakes. I've become a poundcake snob. LOL!

I add some lemon zest, or a full two teaspoons of vanilla extract sometimes. I've also been known to trade the sweet milk, for buttermilk. 

I've made this and the other Grandmother's poundcake from this site over and over and will not use any other recipes for my pound cake.

Great pound cake!! Very buttery!! I did as the reviewers stated and mixed the butter and sugar for 10 minutes, then each egg for 1 minute each, added a Tbs of vanilla after the eggs, substituted heavy cream for the milk and only beat the alternating flour/cream just until combined.

I want to say 1st that I do not like pound cake!!! I made it for my God mother because she requested one and I like to back. I came on this website searching for a repicie and I chose this one. I read all the reviews and after a few alterations, this cake was delicious even for me. My alterations were: I preheated my oven to 325 degrees. I used 2 loaf pans instead of a bundt pan. Eggs and butter must be room temperature! I used one cup of brown sugar and 2 cups of white and creamed with the butter for literally 20min ( I set a timer). Add one egg at a time, 1 min apart. I used 1/2 tablespoon of pure vanilla and 1/2 tablespoon of almond extract. I also put in 1/4 tablespoon of lemon extract. I used cake flour instead of all purpose flour and sifted 3 times before adding in with heavy whipping cream instead of milk. I baked for about an hour. I waited until it completely cooled. Cake came out light brown, full flavored, and delicious.

IT IS CALLED POUND CAKE FOR A REASON! If you rated this 1 or 2 stars, try again and actually weigh out everything! The recipe has been around over a hundred years because it works fine if done correctly. And the instructions could be clearer, also. Start with your eggs. Crack them into a bowl on the scale that has been tared out (google 'how to correctly use a scale' if you don't know what that means.) Use however many eggs it takes to weigh out to 16oz. That way you can use any size eggs you like. Odds are it will not come out to exactly 16 oz, so if you stop at 15.6 oz or go to 17.2 oz, for example, then that tells you how much sugar, butter, and flour to weigh out as well. In the next bowl weigh out that same amount of sugar, and in the next bowl unwrap your sticks of butter and weigh them out also, and adjust to the weight of your eggs by adding a bit more from a 5th stick, or taking out a bit. In the last bowl weigh out your flour. I have never put milk in any pound cake but a lot of recipes that measure it by cups instead of weight usually do add some, but I'd leave it out when you're weighing everything. I would definitely add a half to 1 teaspoon of vanilla and a half to 1 teaspoon of salt as well-every baked good need salt to bring out the sweetness! If you used salted butter you will only need a few pinches of salt. Then proceed as the recipe says by beating the butter and sugar very well until fluffy and most of the sugar is dissolved. Beat in the eggs one at a time as stated, then add any vanilla or other extract and the salt & mix in well. When you are ready to add the flour SIFT it into the batter as you beat it in gently. This will get out any clumps and make it light and fluffy to sprinkle in easily over the batter. This will help keep the pound cake from being too dense. Mix it in gently, just enough to incorporate it. I have never had a problem putting this into an ungreased bundt pan or loaf pans, but you can either grease the pans or use parchment if you prefer. Definitely do the toothpick test after an hour if you've done it in loaf pans and after 70 or 80 minutes if you've done it in a bundt pan. Loaf pans need to cool at least 15 minutes and I'd let a bundt cool at least 20. Give this review a thumbs up if you gave pound cake a 2nd chance and this review helped you get good results :)

I took others' suggestions and added 2tsp vanilla to the batter. Then, I divided the batter into three bowls to make three flavors. One got an extra tsp vanilla, one got a tsp of almond extract, and one got the zest and juice of one lemon plus a lemon glaze. The lemon loaf was beautiful, but the almond loaf was my favorite. They baked in 50-55 minutes--definitely check them well before the 70 minute mark.

This was excellent! I cut the recipe in half (15 servings) and made one loaf in a 9x5 pan. I creamed the butter and sugar for 10 minutes and beat each egg for two minutes after adding, as suggested by other reviews. I also used one teaspoon of vanilla. It took 70 minutes to cook. It was delicious.

OMG - Absolutely delicious! The only changes I made was to halve the recipe and then add 2 tsp lemon extract (3-4 tsp would be even better) between the egg and flour step. I used a 9×6 loaf pan that turned out to be too small! I assumed that without baking soda this wouldn't rise much but it surprisingly did. I cooked at 325° for 80 minutes. Next time I'll bake at 350° in a larger pan and that should reduce the baking time. Because of the high butter content the toothpick test isn't very effective, I removed from oven when center was no longer jiggly and had firmed up. Definitely beat the butter and sugar for at least 10 minutes, an additional 2 minutes with each egg addition and then the bare minimum after you add your flour and milk. So buttery with a light lemon flavor and a nice sweet crust. It didn't even need a glaze!

This turned out really well for me! I added 1 tbsp vanilla, 1/2 tsp almond extracts, sprinkled a little cinnamon and a pinch of salt. Sifted the flour and beat the out of the butter and sugar, until light and fluffy. Initially baked at 350, but noticed it turning dark, so I lowered the temp. It burned a little on top, but that could also be due to baking it in my toaster oven. This will be my go-to recipe for sure!!
Excellent easy cake. I add about 1 tsp vanilla and scant 1/2 tsp salt to half the recipe and bake in one 9” X 5” pan for about 50 minutes. Never fails.

A general time for the oven would have been appreciated. Most pound cakes take about an hour and 15 minutes give or take. It is easy to make. Always match sugar to flour ratio for sweet cake. The batter was very thick and I couldn't pour it. It's baking now so I don't know if that's a good thing or not.

This is the same recipe that has been passed down in my family, except that we add 1 tsp each of vanilla and almond extracts, and bake in a tube pan. I have added green food coloring for St. Patrick's along with a Jameson glaze.... A very versatile cake!!

I made it in a greased and floured Bundt pan instead of loaf pans. My eggs, butter and milk were at room temperature. I added vanilla and it came out with great flavor. I felt it was too much dough for the pan. The top got a little overcooked because it took longer to cook the inside. Can’t wait to make it again and next time, I’ll bake it in my larger tube pan. Great recipe!
this was my first time making something from scratch and it came out nice!! definitely would try again.

The earliest documented recipe for pound cake appears in The Art of Cookery Made Plain and Easy by Hannah Glasse in 1747. While this is the first published recipe, it's believed to have originated in Northern Europe. The cake gained popularity in both England and the United States, with recipes appearing in early American cookbooks as well.
First time with this recipe.. it had a rich dense flavor to it and will definitely be made again
Make this regularly as we have so many eggs !! I add a frozen banana , or lemon rind , or coconut (1/3 c) or slivered almonds . Just made one with chopped up dark chocolate ! Yummy yum
I thought that this was the easiest recipe for pound cake that I’ve seen. The cake came out really good, and my family had nothing but compliments.
